activities.caption: file each tier by what it runs
activities.name: swePyramidSort

config.prompt: File each tier by what it runs:

items.label: one function in isolation — cheap, precise failures
whole system through the UI — slow, brittle, irreplaceable
fail in milliseconds with pinpoint cause
a failing giant tells you only that something, somewhere broke
the middle tier of the shape

config.why: Its shape is an economics argument: hundreds of fast pinpointing checks at the base, a handful of slow whole-system ones at the top.

activities.name: sweTddOrder

config.prompt: Red–green–refactor — put the cycle in order:
items: Refactor, with the suite as the safety net
config.why: A suite is a specification that re-executes on every change — what makes fearless refactoring possible.

activities.anchor: not an argument against knowing where you are going
activities.caption: drag the divider across the planning styles
activities.name: sweAgileCompare

config.prompt: Two planning styles — drag the divider:

before.label: big-design-first
before.text: Plan everything upfront, then build — the empirical failure mode on changing requirements, where the plan and reality drift apart.

after.label: agile iterations
after.text: Short cycles with working software each, re-prioritised against reality — continuous planning rather than no planning.

config.why: Continuous planning replaces upfront planning — the destination stays known; the route gets re-planned.

activities.anchor: you test each midpoint it offers
activities.caption: call the bisect bill
activities.name: sweBisectEst

config.prompt: git bisect binary-searches history between a known-good and a known-bad commit. Roughly how many of its suggested stops localise a regression among 1,000 commits?
config.why: ~10 — the logarithm pointed at your own mistakes.
config.context: A thousand-commit regression collapses to about ten runs.

config.root: 02:14, pages fire: checkout times out. Walk the response.

choices.label: Rollback the deploy from 90 minutes earlier
choices.feedback: Mitigate first: checkout recovers in minutes, and the rollback itself points at the deploy as cause.

choices.label: Start reading code to find the root cause
choices.feedback: Customers bleed while you read: mitigation is minutes, diagnosis is hours — mitigation comes first.

rollback.text: Mitigated. The commit changed a cache key format — a shared cache now misses on every request, and the database, sized for a 90% hit rate, melts at 0%.

choices.label: Ship the fix behind a flag, then run the blameless review
choices.feedback: Tracked actions, not a villain: canary deploys, a cache hit-rate alert, a load test at 0%.

choices.label: Find who pushed the commit and escalate
choices.feedback: A villain hunt teaches everyone to hide mistakes — the review is blameless on purpose.

diagnose.text: Customers bleed while you read: mitigation first, diagnosis second — the sequence exists because minutes beat hours when users wait.

postmortem.text: The pattern generalises: small batches make rollbacks possible; observability makes diagnosis fast; the review converts incidents into permanent defences.

blame.text: A villain hunt teaches everyone to hide mistakes — the review is blameless on purpose.

config.why: Mitigate first, then diagnose — and the review converts each incident into permanent defences.

activities.anchor: is trusted once; the other says
activities.caption: true or false — the estimation folklore
activities.name: sweEstimateJudge

statements.s: A confident single-number estimate is the mark of an experienced engineer.
statements.why: Before the design exists, estimates are routinely 4× wrong either way — a precise date is precision the work cannot support yet.
Agile planning is continuous: short iterations, working software each cycle, re-prioritised against reality.

statements.s: Estimates made before design are routinely 4× wrong in either direction.
statements.why: The cone of uncertainty — estimates tighten only as the design exists.

statements.s: 'Four to eight weeks, and here is what would tell us which' earns more trust than a single promised date.
statements.why: Relative sizing, re-estimating after each increment, and ranges over false certainty — Hofstadter's law is the cone, stated with mercy.

activities.caption: pair each element of the artefact with what it buys
activities.name: sweRepoMatch

config.prompt: Pair each element of the artefact with what it buys:

pairs.right: the ten-minute test — can a new engineer run the checks locally in under ten minutes?
the pipeline is versioned like the code it verifies
style settled by machine, so reviews argue about design
no direct pushes; everything arrives reviewed and green

config.why: Each element removes a category of coordination cost the team would otherwise pay forever.

activities.anchor: The commit convention itself is a skill
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the anatomy of a good message
activities.name: sweCommitCloze

config.text: Subject line in the %%0%% under %%1%% characters ('Fix off-by-one in cart totals'), blank line, then the %%2%% — the what is visible in the diff; only the why needs prose.
config.hint: Read the log: the diary's entries are the message.
